about.title: About Me
about.description: My name is Stefan Vilceanu, and I’m a computer engineer with a passion for drones and autonomous systems. My background spans machine learning, computer vision, robotics, and embedded systems, and I enjoy working across the full stack of technologies, from designing deep learning models and automation pipelines to developing robust software for connected and autonomous systems. I thrive on tackling complex problems, learning new tools and frameworks, and collaborating in multidisciplinary teams to create innovative, reliable solutions that make a difference.

project1.title: Determining Vehicle Position Over Lane Segmentation
project1.tech: YOLOPv2, IPM, Bayesian Filtering, ROS2, Docker
project1.description: The YOLOPv2 model was used for lane line segmentation, IPM was applied to modify the perspective of the image to a Bird's Eye View perspective, and Bayesian Filtering was used to keep the lane localization and assignment algorithm stable.

project2.title: Comparison of Neural Networks for Efficient Inverse Dynamics Identification
project2.description: Developed, trained, tested and compared several neural network architectures for predicting torque in robot joints of a 6-axis industrial robot using the position, velocity and acceleration of the joint as input data.

project3.title: Uncertainty Estimation for 3D Object Detectors
project3.tech: Python, MMDetection, Docker, PETR, ViT, LiDAR, Radar, Camera, Sensor Fusion
project3.description: Analyzed uncertainty estimation in transformer-based 3D object detectors using LiDAR, radar and camera data, evaluating baseline methods against calibration techniques to improve reliabilty without high computational cost.

project4.title: Memristor-based MVM Engine
project4.tech: Cadence, SPICE, C++, Python, Memristor Arrays
project4.description: Built and studied a memristor-based matrix-vector multiplication engine for in-memory computing and compared efficiency, accuracy and resource use to the classical Von Neumann approaches.

project5.title: About The Shape and Texture Bias for Object Recognition
project5.description: Researched about how CNNs, unlike humans, are biased towards textures rathen than shapes when recognizing objects. Additonaly, presented two transformer-based methods to reduce this bias and improve accuracy.

project6.title: Recreating GPT 1 & 2
project6.description: Reimplemented the GPT 1 & 2 architectures from the original OpenAI paper. Trained and tested the models on the Shakespeare and Game of Thrones dataset, in order to let the models produce such-styled content. Similarly, a SIEM query LLM generator was implemented and trained.

project7.title: Inference Pipeline - Autonomous Car
project7.tech: C++, RPi5 & Hailo AI Accelerator, YoloV8, Depth Anything V2
project7.details: For the autonomous RC car project, I designed and built a real-time perception-to-actuation pipeline running on a Raspberry Pi 5 paired with a Hailo-8L AI accelerator, using a custom four-thread C++ architecture that handles image capture, inference, planning, and actuation in parallel for low-latency reaction to the environment; the perception stage runs YOLOv8 for object detection alongside Depth Anything V2 for monocular depth estimation, with the resulting depth data feeding a PD steering controller and PI throttle controller so the car can navigate and avoid obstacles smoothly without dedicated distance sensors, while an autonomous person-following mode built on SORT and ByteTrack multi-object tracking lets the car identify and follow a specific person at a safe distance, all backed by CRSF protocol communication over a 420kbaud hardware UART connected to a RadioMaster RP1/TX12 ELRS transmitter for seamless manual override, and rounded out by hands-free voice control using OpenWakeWord with custom ONNX models (follow-me, stop-engines, three-sixty, autopilot, full-stop) piped into the pipeline via a named FIFO, together forming a complete autonomous driving stack that combines computer vision, depth-based planning, robust RC failover, and voice interaction entirely on embedded edge hardware.
project7.description: Autonomous car built on a RPi 5 and Hailo-8L AI accelerator, combining real-time object detection and monocular depth estimation to enable obstacle-aware navigation and person-following without dedicated distance sensors.

project8.title: Building an FPV Drone
project8.tech: ArduPilot, ELRS, Flight Automation, Flight Controller, Waypoint Navigation, PIDtoolbox
project8.description: Built an FPV drone from scratch, flashing and configuring ArduPilot, ELRS, and the video system. Improved flight performance through blackbox data logging and PID analysis in PIDtoolbox. Configured GPS-based autonomous waypoint navigation with ArduPilot to enable preplanned missions.
